correctness.rationale: The exact two-shore subtraction and sum identities give the unique nonconstant two-color states and existence cutoff. Degree similarity makes the random-walk adjacency symmetric, while bipartiteness gives 2x2 singular-mode blocks and possible unmatched zero modes. The Schur inequalities are explicit affine functions of the squared singular value; q=1 is present on every connected bipartite graph, and q=0 plus q=1 suffice for all modes. The stable interval is exactly the two displayed algebraic roots. SymPy verifies the exact factorization; 16 finite graph eigenvalue cases corroborate, but do not replace, the arbitrary-graph proof.

evidence: Atay--Karabacak 2006 abstract says all bipartite graphs have an identical stability region, but their theorem treats synchronized equilibria and delayed network coupling, whereas the present equilibria are nonhomogeneous. The full paper is paywalled, leaving an explicit comparison risk.
Golubitsky--Stewart 2016 reviews balanced colorings and synchrony patterns without explicit logistic radical thresholds in the inspected abstract.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A theorem about homogeneous synchronized-state stability cannot directly imply linear stability of a state with two distinct local derivatives. The new singular-mode block has different local slopes on the two shores. The original full text of Atay--Karabacak remains an access limitation, not proof of absence.

value.rationale: The exact sharp window holds across arbitrarily sized, degree-heterogeneous undirected bipartite networks without graph-dependent constants, despite isolated population maps being chaotic at multiplier four. Extending an explicit ring pattern to star, path, and arbitrary bipartite networks and proving every transverse perturbation stable in the same interval is structurally meaningful beyond merely substituting a numerical coefficient.
